panels.title: Queue Depth
panels.description: Reconstructions currently queued or pending. High queue depth + slow drain = capacity bottleneck.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) FROM reconstructions WHERE orchestration_status IN ('queued', 'pending');
SELECT count(*) FROM reconstructions WHERE orchestration_status = 'running';
SELECT count(*) FROM reconstructions WHERE orchestration_status = 'succeeded' AND updated_at >= date_trunc('day', now());
SELECT count(*) FROM reconstructions WHERE orchestration_status = 'failed' AND updated_at >= date_trunc('day', now());

panels.title: Median Duration (succeeded)
panels.description: Median time from creation to completion for successful reconstructions

targets.rawSql: SELECT COALESCE(percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (updated_at - created_at))), 0)::int FROM reconstructions WHERE orchestration_status = 'succeeded' AND updated_at > created_at;

panels.title: p95 Duration (succeeded)
panels.description: 95th percentile reconstruction duration. If this is much higher than the median, you have occasional slow reconstructions (likely large capture sessions).

targets.rawSql: SELECT COALESCE(percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (updated_at - created_at))), 0)::int FROM reconstructions WHERE orchestration_status = 'succeeded' AND updated_at > created_at;

panels.title: Reconstruction Duration Over Time
panels.description: Each point is a completed reconstruction. Color indicates success (green) or failure (red). Duration is wall-clock time from creation to final status. Outliers may indicate large capture sessions or resource contention.

targets.rawSql: SELECT updated_at AS time, EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (updated_at - created_at))::int AS "succeeded" FROM reconstructions WHERE orchestration_status = 'succeeded' AND updated_at > created_at ORDER BY updated_at;
SELECT updated_at AS time, EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (updated_at - created_at))::int AS "failed" FROM reconstructions WHERE orchestration_status = 'failed' AND updated_at > created_at ORDER BY updated_at;

panels.title: Duration Percentile Trend (weekly)
panels.description: Rolling weekly percentiles of reconstruction duration. Tracks whether the pipeline is getting faster or slower over time.

targets.rawSql: SELECT date_trunc('week', updated_at) AS time, percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (updated_at - created_at)))::int AS "p50", percentile_cont(0.9) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (updated_at - created_at)))::int AS "p90", percentile_cont(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (updated_at - created_at)))::int AS "p99" FROM reconstructions WHERE orchestration_status = 'succeeded' AND updated_at > created_at AND updated_at >= now() - interval '6 months' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Duration Distribution (histogram buckets)
panels.description: Distribution of reconstruction durations across buckets. Helps identify if you have a bimodal distribution (e.g., quick small sessions + slow large sessions).

targets.rawSql: WITH durations AS (SELECT EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (updated_at - created_at))::int AS dur FROM reconstructions WHERE orchestration_status = 'succeeded' AND updated_at > created_at) SELECT CASE WHEN dur < 60 THEN '<1m' WHEN dur < 300 THEN '1-5m' WHEN dur < 600 THEN '5-10m' WHEN dur < 1800 THEN '10-30m' WHEN dur < 3600 THEN '30-60m' ELSE '>60m' END AS "Duration Bucket", count(*) AS "Count" FROM durations GROUP BY CASE WHEN dur < 60 THEN 1 WHEN dur < 300 THEN 2 WHEN dur < 600 THEN 3 WHEN dur < 1800 THEN 4 WHEN dur < 3600 THEN 5 ELSE 6 END, CASE WHEN dur < 60 THEN '<1m' WHEN dur < 300 THEN '1-5m' WHEN dur < 600 THEN '5-10m' WHEN dur < 1800 THEN '10-30m' WHEN dur < 3600 THEN '30-60m' ELSE '>60m' END ORDER BY 1;

SELECT date_trunc('day', updated_at) AS time, orchestration_status::text AS metric, count(*) AS value FROM reconstructions WHERE orchestration_status IN ('succeeded', 'failed') AND updated_at >= now() - interval '30 days' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Failure Rate by Device Type
panels.description: Failure rate (%) broken down by capture device. If one device type has significantly higher failure rate, it may indicate device-specific issues (frame quality, calibration, etc.).

targets.rawSql: SELECT cs.device_type::text AS device, count(*) AS total, count(*) FILTER (WHERE r.orchestration_status = 'succeeded') AS succeeded, count(*) FILTER (WHERE r.orchestration_status = 'failed') AS failed, CASE WHEN count(*) FILTER (WHERE r.orchestration_status IN ('succeeded', 'failed')) = 0 THEN 0 ELSE round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE r.orchestration_status = 'failed') / count(*) FILTER (WHERE r.orchestration_status IN ('succeeded', 'failed')), 1) END AS failure_rate_pct, COALESCE(avg(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (r.updated_at - r.created_at))) FILTER (WHERE r.orchestration_status = 'succeeded'), 0)::int AS avg_duration_sec FROM reconstructions r JOIN capture_sessions cs ON cs.id = r.capture_session_id GROUP BY cs.device_type ORDER BY failure_rate_pct DESC;

panels.title: Retry Analysis: Reconstructions per Capture Session
panels.description: Captures with multiple reconstruction attempts. High retry counts indicate persistent issues with specific capture data.

targets.rawSql: SELECT cs.name AS capture_session, cs.device_type::text AS device, count(r.id) AS attempts, count(r.id) FILTER (WHERE r.orchestration_status = 'succeeded') AS succeeded, count(r.id) FILTER (WHERE r.orchestration_status = 'failed') AS failed, min(r.created_at) AS first_attempt, max(r.updated_at) AS last_attempt FROM capture_sessions cs JOIN reconstructions r ON r.capture_session_id = cs.id GROUP BY cs.id, cs.name, cs.device_type HAVING count(r.id) > 1 ORDER BY count(r.id) DESC LIMIT 20;

panels.title: Failed Reconstructions Detail
panels.description: Recent failed reconstructions with timing and capture details. Use this to identify patterns in failures.

targets.rawSql: SELECT r.id AS reconstruction_id, cs.name AS capture_session, cs.device_type::text AS device, r.orchestration_status::text AS status, r.created_at, r.updated_at, EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (r.updated_at - r.created_at))::int AS duration_sec, (SELECT count(*) FROM reconstructions r2 WHERE r2.capture_session_id = r.capture_session_id) AS total_attempts FROM reconstructions r JOIN capture_sessions cs ON cs.id = r.capture_session_id WHERE r.orchestration_status = 'failed' ORDER BY r.updated_at DESC LIMIT 30;

panels.title: Reconstructor Feature Extraction Log
panels.description: Live log stream of feature extraction progress from the reconstructor. Pattern: 'Extracting features: image N of M'

panels.title: Reconstruction State Transitions Over Time
panels.description: Weekly count of reconstructions by final state. Helps identify periods of instability.

targets.rawSql: SELECT date_trunc('week', updated_at) AS time, orchestration_status::text AS metric, count(*) AS value FROM reconstructions WHERE orchestration_status IN ('succeeded', 'failed', 'cancelled') AND updated_at >= now() - interval '6 months' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Failure Rate Trend (weekly %)
panels.description: Weekly failure rate as a percentage. A rising trend indicates systematic issues.

targets.rawSql: SELECT date_trunc('week', updated_at) AS time, CASE WHEN count(*) = 0 THEN 0 ELSE round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE orchestration_status = 'failed') / count(*), 1) END AS "Failure Rate %" FROM reconstructions WHERE orchestration_status IN ('succeeded', 'failed') AND updated_at >= now() - interval '6 months' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
